definitions.explanation: To not like something or someone.

examples.japanese: ⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{嫌|きら}い⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
{嫌|きら}いな⟦{食|た}べ{物|もの}→食べ物：02890_tabemono⟧
⟦{勉強|べんきょう}→勉強：00770_benkyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{嫌|きら}い⟦じゃない→じゃない：28483_janai⟧。
{嫌|きら}いな⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いません→いる：00495_iru⟧。

examples.english: I disliked fish as a child, but now I like it.

notes:
{嫌|きら}い is a na-adjective expressing dislike. Unlike English "hate," it covers mild dislikes as well as strong ones, so it is the ordinary word for "I don't like it."

FORMS:
- {嫌|きら}い⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧: (I) dislike
- {嫌|きら}いな + noun: disliked ~
- {嫌|きら}いではない / {嫌|きら}い⟦じゃない→じゃない：28483_janai⟧: don't dislike

INTENSITY SCALE:
- ⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧: like
- {嫌|きら}い⟦じゃない→じゃない：28483_janai⟧: don't dislike
- {嫌|きら}い: dislike
- ⟦{大嫌|だいきら}い→大嫌い：12178_daikirai⟧: really hate

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{嫌|きら}い: dislike ~
- {嫌|きら}い⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to come to dislike
- {嫌|きら}いではありません: I don't dislike (polite denial)
⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ marks what is disliked: ⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{嫌|きら}い (dislike vegetables). The topic marker ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ replaces ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ when the item is contrasted with something else: ⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{嫌|きら}い⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧ (vegetables, at least, I don't like).

CAUTION — PEOPLE:
Saying {嫌|きら}い directly about a person is blunt and can sound harsh. In conversation speakers usually soften it: ⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧ (not comfortable with), あまり{好|す}きではない (not very fond of), or ⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧⟦じゃない→じゃない：28483_janai⟧.

CONTRAST WITH ⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧:
{嫌|きら}い states an emotional dislike; ⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧ says the speaker is bad at something or ill at ease with it, and is the politer choice for foods, subjects, and people.
